subject: music
title: Elements Foundations: Pitch, Duration & Dynamics
welcome_lead: Meet the building blocks every musician uses — pitch, duration and dynamics.
meta_desc: GCSE Music Musical Elements Adventure 1: foundations of pitch, duration, dynamics and how to describe music precisely.
final_note: You can now describe any music using the basic three elements.

concepts.def: How high or low a sound is.
How loud or quiet music is.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pitch is determined by frequency — fast vibrations = high pitch, slow = low. We describe melodies as ascending or descending, with narrow or wide range.

Each instrument has its own range — a piccolo plays high, a tuba plays low. Composers choose registers to create colour and balance.

Duration tells us how long sounds and silences last. The note values — semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver — give us a vocabulary for time.

Combined into patterns, durations form rhythm. Hold time over a regular pulse = a beat; the way beats are grouped = a metre (e.g. 4/4).

The standard ladder: pp (pianissimo) – p (piano) – mp (mezzo-piano) – mf (mezzo-forte) – f (forte) – ff (fortissimo).

Crescendo (cresc.) = gradually louder; diminuendo (dim.) = gradually quieter. Sudden changes use sforzando (sfz) — a sharp accent.
